links.outcome: Spearman correlation with PDFF versus existing foundation models and clinical risk scores
links.effect: Bioprofile models achieved a Spearman coefficient of 0.65 against PDFF, outperforming existing foundation models (ρ = 0.361) and clinical risk scores (ρ = 0.522-0.542) in retrospective validation.
links.quote: Bioprofile models achieved a Spearman coefficient of 0.65 against PDFF, outperforming existing foundation models (ρ = 0.361) and clinical risk scores (ρ = 0.522-0.542) in retrospective validation.

unlisted_practices: Using AI patient representations to nominate candidates for clinical study recruitment to reduce screening failures

screen.reason: Prospective clinical pilot evaluating a physiological foundation model ('Bioprofile') to identify and recruit candidates with subclinical steatotic liver disease for clinical studies, but it evaluates the model's predictive performance rather than testing a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
